items.title: Vercel ships Security Review (public beta): scans every GitHub push for vulnerabilities, fixes in one click via Vercel Agent
items.summary: New capability in Vercel Agent, alongside Code Review and Investigation. Scans for vulnerabilities on every push to a team's connected GitHub repos, surfaces findings in the Security dashboard, PR comments and the CLI, and with permission Vercel Agent can validate and push a fix.
items.why: A scan-plus-autonomous-fix loop wired directly into your push pipeline is the kind of agentic guardrail most teams are still hand-rolling themselves.
items.action: If you're on Vercel Pro/Enterprise, turn on Security Review in Vercel Agent Settings for one repo and see what it flags on your next push, reviews are free until Nov 10.

items.title: OpenAI's security team ran an autonomous pipeline that found and patched 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation bugs in one run
items.summary: An upcoming OpenAI cyber model discovered, validated, and generated patches for 948 local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel in a single run, at a total API cost of $1.2 million.
items.why: This is what an autonomous find-exploit-patch loop looks like at kernel scale right now, a preview of both the ceiling and the price tag for agentic vulnerability remediation.
items.action: Not a tool you can use today, but worth copying the shape: validate the bug is real, patch it, then re-verify, the same structure any autonomous code-fix step in your own harness should have.

items.title: New paper: coding agents can't reliably tell when their own work is wrong
items.summary: A new benchmark chains 20 consecutive real-world requests per project across 140 open-source repos. Ten coding agents complete 95% of requests taken one at a time, but only 51% when chained, because they miss their own mistakes and later requests build on the broken result. Asked directly whether their own implementation is correct, agents are right 53% of the time. One external correction plus a repair round lifts chain completion from 51% to 59%.
items.why: Real numbers behind something worth internalizing: an agent's own confidence, and its own passing tests, aren't a trustworthy stop signal for a chain of work, you need an outside check.
items.action: If you're chaining agent requests in your own harness, add one deliberate external verification step between requests instead of trusting the agent's own done signal.
